newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court sentences 31 more students.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court sentences 31 more students.

text.p: A South Korean court on Monday jailed 15 students and gave suspended prison terms to 16 others for their roles in violent pro-North Korean campus protests in August, a court official said.

This brings to 220 the number of students sentenced in connection with the demonstrations at Seoul's Yonsei University in which one riot policeman was killed and hundreds of other officers and students injured.

The 15 students were jailed for between 10 months and two years for taking part in an illegal protest, engaging in acts of violence and obstructing police in their duty, the official said. Suspended sentences were for two years.
A total of 444 students were sent to trial in batches at different courthouses.

Riot police stormed Yonsei to end a seven-day occupation of two teaching blocks by students involved in an annual pro-Korean unification rally and calling for the withdrawal of 37,000 U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.
The riot policeman died in pitched fighting during which students used petrol bombs, iron pipes and stones.
